subject: Neurology
vignette: A 4-year-old girl has a port-wine stain involving the left forehead and upper eyelid. She has developed seizures and mild left-sided weakness. Imaging shows ipsilateral leptomeningeal angiomas with calcifications, and her intraocular pressure is elevated.
question: Which of the following best describes this disorder?

options.text: Autosomal dominant TSC2 mutation with ash-leaf spots and cardiac rhabdomyoma
NF1 with cafe-au-lait spots and Lisch nodules
VHL with hemangioblastomas and renal cell carcinoma
Somatic mosaic activating GNAQ mutation causing a port-wine stain in V1/V2 and ipsilateral leptomeningeal angioma

explanation_correct: Sturge-Weber syndrome, or encephalotrigeminal angiomatosis, is a congenital nonhereditary anomaly of neural crest derivatives caused by somatic mosaicism for an activating GNAQ mutation. It produces a port-wine stain in the CN V1/V2 distribution with an ipsilateral leptomeningeal angioma that calcifies, leading to seizures, intellectual disability, and early-onset glaucoma from an episcleral hemangioma.

explanation_incorrect.A: Tuberous sclerosis is an autosomal dominant TSC1/TSC2 disorder with ash-leaf spots, angiofibromas, and cardiac rhabdomyoma rather than a port-wine stain.
explanation_incorrect.B: Neurofibromatosis type 1 features cafe-au-lait spots, neurofibromas, and Lisch nodules, not a facial capillary malformation and leptomeningeal angioma.
explanation_incorrect.C: Von Hippel-Lindau disease features hemangioblastomas, angiomatosis, and bilateral renal cell carcinomas with a germline VHL deletion.
explanation_incorrect.E: Neurofibromatosis type 2 causes bilateral vestibular schwannomas and juvenile cataracts due to a merlin mutation on chromosome 22.

educationalObjective: Identify Sturge-Weber syndrome by somatic GNAQ mosaicism, V1/V2 port-wine stain, and ipsilateral leptomeningeal angioma.

subject: Neurology
vignette: A 3-year-old boy has multiple hypopigmented ash-leaf spots and facial angiofibromas. He has a history of seizures and a cardiac rhabdomyoma. Renal imaging shows bilateral angiomyolipomas.
question: Which of the following genes is most commonly associated with this condition?
explanation_correct: Tuberous sclerosis complex is an autosomal dominant disorder with variable expression caused by mutations in the tumor suppressor genes TSC1 on chromosome 9 encoding hamartin and TSC2 on chromosome 16 encoding tuberin. It produces hamartomas in the CNS and skin with ash-leaf spots, angiofibromas, shagreen patches, cardiac rhabdomyoma, renal angiomyolipoma, and seizures.

explanation_incorrect.A: NF1 encodes neurofibromin on chromosome 17 and causes cafe-au-lait spots and neurofibromas, not ash-leaf spots and renal angiomyolipomas.
explanation_incorrect.C: VHL on chromosome 3p causes hemangioblastomas and bilateral renal cell carcinoma rather than this hamartoma syndrome.
explanation_incorrect.D: GNAQ somatic mosaicism causes Sturge-Weber syndrome with a port-wine stain, not tuberous sclerosis.
explanation_incorrect.E: NF2 encodes merlin on chromosome 22 and causes bilateral vestibular schwannomas, not the findings described.

educationalObjective: Link tuberous sclerosis to TSC1 hamartin and TSC2 tuberin with characteristic skin and visceral hamartomas.

subject: Neurology
vignette: A 9-year-old boy has more than six cafe-au-lait spots, multiple cutaneous neurofibromas, and pigmented iris hamartomas. He has an optic glioma and a family history of similar lesions in an autosomal dominant pattern with complete penetrance.
question: Which of the following best describes the molecular defect in this disorder?

options.text: pVHL that ubiquitinates HIF1-alpha on chromosome 3p
Neurofibromin, a negative regulator of RAS, encoded by NF1 on chromosome 17

explanation_correct: Neurofibromatosis type 1 is autosomal dominant with 100% penetrance and results from mutation of the NF1 tumor suppressor gene on chromosome 17, which encodes neurofibromin, a negative regulator of RAS. Its features are remembered by CICLOPSS: cafe-au-lait spots, intellectual disability, cutaneous neurofibromas, Lisch nodules, optic glioma, pheochromocytoma, seizures or focal signs, and bone lesions.

explanation_incorrect.A: Merlin is the NF2 gene product on chromosome 22 and causes bilateral vestibular schwannomas rather than NF1.
explanation_incorrect.B: pVHL is the product of the VHL gene on chromosome 3p that ubiquitinates HIF1-alpha and causes von Hippel-Lindau disease.
explanation_incorrect.D: Tuberin is encoded by TSC2 on chromosome 16 and is associated with tuberous sclerosis complex.
explanation_incorrect.E: An activating GNAQ somatic mutation causes the port-wine stain of Sturge-Weber syndrome, not neurofibromatosis.

educationalObjective: Understand NF1 as a chromosome 17 neurofibromin mutation that normally restrains RAS signaling.

subject: Neurology
vignette: A 28-year-old woman presents with bilateral sensorineural hearing loss and tinnitus. Imaging reveals bilateral vestibular schwannomas. She also has juvenile cataracts and a meningioma.
question: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation_correct: Neurofibromatosis type 2 is an autosomal dominant disorder caused by mutation of the NF2 tumor suppressor gene encoding merlin on chromosome 22. It is characterized by bilateral vestibular schwannomas, juvenile cataracts, meningiomas, and ependymomas, remembered as affecting 2 ears and 2 eyes. Bilateral vestibular schwannomas are essentially diagnostic.

explanation_incorrect.B: Neurofibromatosis type 1 causes cafe-au-lait spots, cutaneous neurofibromas, and Lisch nodules rather than bilateral vestibular schwannomas.
explanation_incorrect.C: Tuberous sclerosis complex presents with ash-leaf spots, angiofibromas, seizures, and visceral hamartomas, not vestibular schwannomas.
explanation_incorrect.D: Von Hippel-Lindau disease features hemangioblastomas, angiomatosis, bilateral renal cell carcinoma, and pheochromocytoma.
explanation_incorrect.E: Sturge-Weber syndrome presents with a facial port-wine stain, leptomeningeal angioma, seizures, and glaucoma in a somatic mosaic pattern.

educationalObjective: Recognize NF2 by bilateral vestibular schwannomas and juvenile cataracts from a merlin mutation on chromosome 22.

subject: Neurology
vignette: A 35-year-old man with a family history of renal cancer presents with a cerebellar hemangioblastoma and retinal angiomas. Further workup reveals a pheochromocytoma.
question: Which of the following best describes the genetic mechanism in this disorder?

options.text: TSC1 mutation with loss of hamartin
NF2 mutation with loss of merlin
NF1 mutation with loss of neurofibromin
Deletion of VHL on chromosome 3p; pVHL normally ubiquitinates HIF1-alpha

explanation_correct: Von Hippel-Lindau disease is autosomal dominant from deletion of the VHL gene on chromosome 3p. The pVHL protein normally ubiquitinates hypoxia-inducible factor 1-alpha, and its loss leads to HARP: hemangioblastomas of the retina, brainstem, cerebellum, and spine, angiomatosis, bilateral renal cell carcinomas, and pheochromocytoma.

explanation_incorrect.A: TSC1 mutation causes tuberous sclerosis with hamartin loss and hamartomas such as ash-leaf spots and renal angiomyolipomas, not hemangioblastomas.
explanation_incorrect.B: NF2 mutation with merlin loss causes bilateral vestibular schwannomas and juvenile cataracts rather than retinal and cerebellar tumors.
explanation_incorrect.C: NF1 mutation with neurofibromin loss causes cafe-au-lait spots and neurofibromas, not the HARP tumor spectrum.
explanation_incorrect.D: Activating GNAQ somatic mutation underlies Sturge-Weber syndrome with a port-wine stain and leptomeningeal angioma.

educationalObjective: Understand VHL as a chromosome 3p deletion impairing HIF1-alpha ubiquitination and causing hemangioblastomas and bilateral RCC.

subject: Neurology
vignette: A 2-year-old boy with ash-leaf spots and shagreen patches develops seizures. Imaging reveals a tumor arising near the foramen of Monro. His mother has facial angiofibromas and ungual fibromas.
question: Which of the following tumor types is specifically associated with this condition?
explanation_correct: Tuberous sclerosis complex has an increased incidence of subependymal giant cell astrocytoma, which typically arises near the foramen of Monro, as well as ungual fibromas. The diagnosis is supported by ash-leaf spots, shagreen patches, angiofibromas, seizures, and a family history consistent with autosomal dominant TSC1 or TSC2 mutation.

explanation_incorrect.A: Optic glioma is associated with neurofibromatosis type 1, not tuberous sclerosis.
explanation_incorrect.C: Vestibular schwannoma, especially bilateral, is characteristic of neurofibromatosis type 2.
explanation_incorrect.D: Hemangioblastoma is the characteristic CNS tumor of von Hippel-Lindau disease.
explanation_incorrect.E: A colloid cyst is a benign third ventricular lesion that causes obstructive hydrocephalus and is not a neurocutaneous tumor.

educationalObjective: Associate subependymal giant cell astrocytoma with tuberous sclerosis complex and its family of hamartomatous tumors.

subject: Neurology
vignette: A newborn girl is noted to have a flat, reddish-brown birthmark involving the skin over her left forehead and upper eyelid. Her parents are concerned about possible associated neurologic and ocular complications.
question: Which of the following additional findings would most strongly suggest Sturge-Weber syndrome?

options.text: Ipsilateral leptomeningeal angioma with calcifications and early-onset glaucoma

explanation_correct: Sturge-Weber syndrome features a port-wine stain in the CN V1/V2 distribution with an ipsilateral leptomeningeal angioma that develops calcifications, producing seizures and intellectual disability. An episcleral hemangioma can raise intraocular pressure and cause early-onset glaucoma, making this combination the most specific association.

explanation_incorrect.A: Bilateral vestibular schwannomas are characteristic of neurofibromatosis type 2, not Sturge-Weber syndrome.
explanation_incorrect.B: Cafe-au-lait spots and Lisch nodules are features of neurofibromatosis type 1.
explanation_incorrect.D: Renal angiomyolipomas and cardiac rhabdomyomas are features of tuberous sclerosis complex.
explanation_incorrect.E: Retinal hemangioblastomas are associated with von Hippel-Lindau disease.

educationalObjective: Link a V1/V2 port-wine stain with ipsilateral leptomeningeal angioma and early glaucoma to Sturge-Weber syndrome.
